# Installing a stack {#sec-install}

Each install path (an "arm") starts from a bare `ubuntu:24.04` container, with no Python and no
curl, and runs the same probe: a Copernicus 30 m DEM COG read over HTTPS, warped to a 40 km
Australian Albers box at 40 m (bilinear), plus the versions, the drivers, and the shared
libraries loaded in the process.

## The default against pixi

| | **A: venv + pip** | **B: pixi** |
|---|---|---|
| Install | apt python3-venv; `pip install rasterio numpy geopandas matplotlib` | apt curl; pixi; `pixi add python numpy gdal libgdal r-base r-gdalraster r-vapour r-wk`; ximage from CRAN |
| Wall time (fast link) | ~45 s | ~30 s |
| Disk | 555 MB (Python only) | 1.8 GB (Python **and** R) |
| GDAL | 3.12.2 (rasterio), 3.12.4 (pyogrio) | 3.13.3 |
| libgdal copies in one process | **2**, different versions (also 2 PROJ, 2 GEOS) | **1**, the same file for Python and R |
| `osgeo.gdal` | not available: no wheel on PyPI; `pip install gdal` fails without `gdal-config` | yes, including `gdal.Run()` (the new CLI as an API) |
| Drivers missing (of 21 checked) | Parquet, FlatGeobuf, OpenFileGDB, KEA, PostgreSQL, LIBKML | Parquet only; none with `libgdal-arrow-parquet` |
| DEM warp mean | 558.9196 | 558.9198, identical across osgeo.gdal, gdalraster, vapour |

Getting `osgeo.gdal` into arm A the hard way (apt `libgdal-dev g++ python3-dev`, then
`pip install gdal==3.8.4`, then a `--no-build-isolation` rebuild to get `gdal_array`) took 82 s
of apt alone and gave GDAL 3.8.4 with no `gdal.Run`.

The warp means differ in the fourth decimal place. That isn't a difference between the
bindings, it's a GDAL version change, and [chapter @sec-one-gdal] explains it.

## Python only, like for like

The same clean image, Python only. "Install" excludes the apt step, which varied from 16 s to
124 s with mirror load.

| | A: venv + pip | B-py core | B-py | B-py like-for-like |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Packages | rasterio numpy geopandas matplotlib | python numpy gdal matplotlib-base | + libgdal | + libgdal rasterio geopandas |
| Install | 22 s (venv + pip) | 5 s | 5 s | 7 s |
| Env on disk | 534 MB | 626 MB | 934 MB | 1.19 GB |
| Files in env | 9,296 | 14,147 | 23,173 | 31,657 |
| Env + download cache | 677 MB | 770 MB | 1.21 GB | 1.50 GB |
| GDAL drivers | 147 (rasterio) | 191 | 210 | 210 |
| `osgeo.gdal` | no | yes | yes | yes |
| libgdal copies in one process | 2 (3.12.2, 3.12.4) | 1 | 1 | **1**: rasterio and pyogrio both on 3.13.3 |

- **On disk, pip is smaller:** 534 MB against 626 MB for core GDAL, or 934 MB with every plugin.
  The pixi env has 1.5 to 2.5 times as many files, which matters under HPC file-count quotas.
- **pixi is faster once apt is done**, because it downloads prebuilt packages in parallel and
  hardlinks them from its cache.
- **conda-forge also removes the duplicate GDAL for rasterio users.** In the like-for-like env,
  rasterio 1.5.2 and pyogrio load the env's single libgdal 3.13.3. The duplicate comes from the
  wheels, not from rasterio.

## The R side

A newcomer installs `sf terra gdalraster vapour wk ximage jsonlite` on a bare `ubuntu:24.04`
with `install.packages()`, three ways, against the pixi env.

| | CRAN source | Posit P3M binaries | r2u | pixi |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Setup | `apt install r-base` (130-254 s, pulls compilers) | same, plus a repo URL and an `HTTPUserAgent` option | r2u script: CRAN apt repo, bspm (59 s) | pixi (shared with Python) |
| First `install.packages()` | 87-253 s; **3 of 7 load**: sf, terra, gdalraster, vapour fail (no system libraries) | **3 of 7 load**: binaries install without error, then won't load (no libgdal etc.) | **7 of 7** in 36 s | 7 of 7 |
| Fix | 8 `-dev` packages, then 535 s compiling: **6 of 7**. sf still fails: s2 needs Abseil (`libabsl-dev`) or cmake, which the usual list omits | 4 runtime libraries from apt, then 19 s: 7 of 7 | none | none |
| R | 4.3.3 | 4.3.3 | 4.6.2 | 4.5.3 |
| GDAL / PROJ / GEOS | 3.8.4 / 9.4.0 / 3.12.1 (Ubuntu) | same | same | 3.13.3 / 9.9.0 / 3.15.0 |
| One libgdal for every package | yes | yes | yes | yes, **and shared with Python** |
| DEM warp, gdalraster and vapour | 558.9196 | 558.9196 | 558.9196 | 558.9198 |
| DEM warp, `terra::project` | 558.9181 | 558.9181 | 558.9181 | not run |

- **On Linux, R already has the "one GDAL" property:** every package links the system libgdal.
  R's problems are the setup cliff (two of three default paths fail first, silently in P3M's
  case) and the **age** of Ubuntu's GDAL (3.8.4, released February 2024).
- **r2u is the strongest R default on Ubuntu:** one script, then binaries for everything, with
  system libraries pulled in by apt. It's limited to Ubuntu LTS and to the distro's GDAL.
- **The source path's documented system requirements are out of date for sf**, because of s2
  and Abseil. A newcomer following them ends up with no sf.
- `terra::project` gives a different answer from `gdal.Warp`, gdalraster and vapour **on the same
  GDAL** (mean 558.9181 against 558.9196; min and max agree). Not yet explained.

## Everything from apt

Add `python3-gdal` to r2u and Ubuntu alone gives a complete stack: Python and R load the
distro's one libgdal, nothing compiles, and there is no venv.

| | Ubuntu 24.04 | Ubuntu 26.04 | pixi, 26.04, for scale |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDAL / Python / R | 3.8.4 / 3.12 / 4.6.2 | 3.12.2 / 3.14.4 / 4.6.2 | 3.13.3 / 3.15.2 / 4.5.3 |
| R packages that load | 7 of 7 | 7 of 7 | 7 of 7 |
| Time / disk | apt + r2u + 3 R packages about 2.2 min | about 3.3 min, 591 MB in total | 1.8 GB env + 309 MB cache |
| Drivers missing (of 21) | not probed | Parquet, KEA | Parquet |
| DEM warp mean | 558.9196 | 558.9196 | 558.9198 |

The warp mean follows the GDAL version, not the installer. The distro's GDAL turned out to be
enough for all four real projects in [Part II](projects.qmd). Where it falls short is anything
needing Parquet (DEA's STAC-GeoParquet indexes) and GDAL's STACIT driver, which on 3.8.4 can't
read current DEA items.

## Choosing GDAL plugins on conda-forge

conda-forge's `gdal` package pulls in only `libgdal-core`, without netCDF, HDF5, JP2, KEA, PDF,
PostgreSQL or Parquet. `libgdal` adds all but Parquet, which is separate because of Arrow.
Python only, `matplotlib-base`, clean `ubuntu:24.04`:

| GDAL packages | Env | Files | Drivers | Missing from the 21 checked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gdal` (= libgdal-core) | 626 MB | 14k | 191 | netCDF, HDF5, Parquet, JP2, KEA, PDF, PostgreSQL |
| `gdal libgdal-netcdf libgdal-hdf5 libgdal-jp2openjpeg libgdal-arrow-parquet` | 845 MB | 18k | 203 | KEA, PDF, PostgreSQL |
| `gdal libgdal` | 934 MB | 23k | 210 | Parquet |
| **`gdal libgdal libgdal-arrow-parquet`** | **1.02 GB** | **24k** | **212** | none |
| pip: rasterio + geopandas wheels, for scale | 534 MB | 9k | 147 | Parquet, FlatGeobuf, OpenFileGDB, KEA, PostgreSQL, LIBKML |

Most of the size is cloud SDKs (gRPC, Google Cloud, AWS, protobuf). TileDB and Arrow both pull
them in, so the trimmed set saves only 170 MB. Default to all plugins; use the trimmed set when
files or space are tight. The Parquet driver reads the ga-sar-ice EW STAC-GeoParquet index over
HTTPS in under a second (190 scenes, 149 fields).

Use `matplotlib-base`, not `matplotlib`: on conda-forge, `matplotlib` pulls in Qt6, PySide6,
LLVM and Clang (about 150 MB compressed). With it the Python-only env was 1.7 GB and 36k files;
without it, 934 MB.

A starting `pixi.toml` is in [chapter @sec-guidelines].
